## Verdict: not impacted

`bikini/exploitarium` is a dump of ~44 self-published PoCs (4.1k stars, 12 assigned CVEs in `cves.md`, the rest claimed as unreported). I enumerated the actual directory listing via the GitHub API rather than trusting the page summary, then checked each entry against DataQ's real dependency graph. Nothing lands.

**The four entries that touch our stack, and why each misses:**

| PoC | Our reality | Why not exploitable |
|---|---|---|
| `redis-vset-duplicate-hnsw-id-rce` | `redis:7-alpine` (compose + [redis.tf:43](deploy/terraform/azure/redis.tf#L43)) | Bug is in the **Vector Sets module**, bundled from Redis **8**. Redis 7 has no `VSET`/`VLINKS` surface at all. Also needs an authenticated client: our broker is `external_enabled = false` + `--requirepass`. |
| `postgres-ri-owner-switched-cast` | PG 16 local / Azure Flexible Server prod | Needs a **hostile DB role** that can `CREATE TYPE/FUNCTION/CAST` and holds `REFERENCES`, *plus* a referenced-table owner in `pg_execute_server_program`. We have one least-priv `dataq_app` role and no untrusted roles; Azure doesn't grant `pg_execute_server_program`. Tested against 20devel. |
| `curl-smtp-expn-recipient-crlf-injection` | [email.py:316](backend/app/alerting/email.py#L316) uses Python `smtplib`, not libcurl | Not the same code path — and the analogous risk in *our* code is already closed: user-supplied recipients are CRLF-rejected at write time by `_UNSAFE_IN_RECIPIENT` ([notification_service.py:120](backend/app/services/notification_service.py#L120), from the #639 review). |
| `flowise-mcp-env-case-bypass` | Our MCP is a FastMCP **server** at `/mcp` | Flowise spawns stdio children from user config with an env denylist; we never spawn a child process from user input and have no env denylist. |

That last one is a class worth checking rather than a package match — a case-**sensitive** list matched against a case-**insensitive** value. I audited our three such lists and all normalize both sides: webhook SSRF hosts lowercase config ([:58](backend/app/services/notification_service.py#L58)) *and* parsed host ([:83](backend/app/services/notification_service.py#L83)), and the workspace-admin allowlist matches case-insensitively ([auth.py:283](backend/app/core/auth.py#L283)). They're allowlists too, so the failure mode is fail-closed.

**Confirmed absent from the graph:** Pillow, pycurl, pycares/aiodns, paramiko/ssh2, libarchive (`pnpm audit`-relevant Next.js too — we're Vite). `nghttpx` and `docker cp` appear nowhere in the repo. The remaining ~35 PoCs are desktop/unrelated-server software (Firefox, ffmpeg, VLC, Ghidra, QEMU, nmap, objdump, 7zip, AnyDesk, RustDesk, Discord, Discourse, Gogs, Gitea, NodeBB, MyBB, NextCloud, PHP, OpenVPN, SystemInformer) — no intersection with DataQ or its CI.

**Two things to carry forward, not act on now:**

1. **Redis 8 is now a gated upgrade.** If we ever bump `redis:7-alpine` → 8, the vector-sets module arrives with it and this becomes live-relevant (no vendor fix exists). Cheap mitigation if we do: don't load the module, keep `--requirepass` + internal ingress.
2. **The Postgres finding is a "don't ever hand out DB roles" constraint.** Our safety here is the single-role model, not a patch. Relevant if multi-tenant DB access is ever considered.

Two honest caveats: these are largely **unpatched** issues, so "not impacted" rests on non-intersection and missing preconditions rather than on us being up to date — there's nothing to bump. And I've taken the repo's technical claims at face value for the impact analysis; I didn't run any PoC. That doesn't change the conclusion, since non-intersection holds whether or not the bugs are real.

No issue filed and no code changed — there's no finding to fix. Say the word if you'd like me to record the Redis-8 gate as a note in `CLAUDE.md` §11 or as a GitHub issue so it isn't rediscovered at upgrade time.

1	# Security & data handling
2	
3	How DataQ authenticates users, stores secrets, handles the data it sees, and what it keeps.
4	This is a plain-language overview for people evaluating or operating DataQ. It is **not** a
5	legal compliance certification — much of GDPR/HIPAA is organizational (DPAs, BAAs, consent,
6	lawful basis) and is the deploying organization's responsibility.
7	
8	## Authentication & access
9	
10	- **Single sign-on (OIDC).** Users sign in through your identity provider; DataQ is
11	  provider-neutral (validated against Azure AD). The backend validates the token on every
12	  request — there is no local password store.
13	- **Personal access tokens (PATs).** For headless / AI-client use, users mint `dq_live_`
14	  tokens ([API keys](api-keys.md)). Tokens are **hashed (SHA-256) at rest** — the plaintext is
15	  shown once and never stored — and carry the **same authz as the user**, on REST and MCP.
16	  They can be scoped with an expiry and revoked.
17	- **Per-suite authorization.** Access is granted per suite (**view / edit**); a caller only
18	  ever sees suites they own or are shared on. There are no ambient "see everything" reads
19	  except the workspace-admin role below.
20	- **Workspace admins.** An allowlisted role (`WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS`) with workspace-wide
21	  visibility over every suite, its results, and schedules (ADR 0027). Because that includes
22	  failing-row samples (the one place PII can appear), **keep the allowlist minimal** and treat
23	  a data-access audit trail as a prerequisite before granting it in a regulated deployment.
24	
25	## Network exposure
26	
27	- The **frontend is the only public surface**; the API runs on **internal ingress** and is
28	  reached only through the frontend's same-origin `/api`, `/healthz`, and `/mcp` proxy
29	  (ADR 0028 §5). All traffic is over **HTTPS/TLS**.
30	- The **MCP** AI-assistant endpoint is **fail-closed** — unauthenticated requests are rejected
31	  (ADR 0008).
32	
33	## Secrets
34	
35	- Datasource credentials, webhook signing keys, and channel secrets are held in a **secret
36	  store behind a seam** — Azure Key Vault in the reference deployment — never in the database
37	  or in git. The app reads them via a managed identity.
38	- Secret **references** (names), not secret values, are stored alongside connections. Deleting
39	  a connection removes its secret (soft-delete on Key Vault).
40	- Inbound webhooks are authenticated: ADF by a shared secret, Airflow and dbt by an
41	  **HMAC-SHA256** signature keyed on a stored signing key.
42	
43	## The data DataQ sees, stores, and redacts
44	
45	DataQ runs checks *against* your data; it is **not** a copy of your data. What it persists:
46	
47	- **Metadata** — suites, checks, connection config (no secrets), schedules, trigger bindings.
48	- **Results** — per-check pass/fail + a numeric `metric_value`, and for failing checks a
49	  small **failing-row sample**.
50	- **Failing-row samples are the one place results can carry PII/PHI.** They are **redacted at
51	  the boundary, column-aware**: a suite's **column policy** (auto-derived by a classifier or
52	  set by hand) keeps non-sensitive breach values debuggable while masking PII columns to
53	  `<redacted>`. The numeric counts and row/column shape are kept.
54	- **Logs & traces** are PII-redacted at the logger level, and secret values never enter them.
55	
56	## Retention
57	
58	- Failing-row **samples are purged** after a retention window (PII-minimisation), while the
59	  aggregatable **`metric_value` history is kept** for trends and baselines — so you lose the
60	  raw rows but keep the signal.
61	
62	## Encryption
63	
64	- **In transit:** HTTPS/TLS everywhere (public ingress and the internal proxy hop).
65	- **At rest:** provided by the managed data services — PostgreSQL, the object stores, and Key
66	  Vault all encrypt at rest in the reference (Azure) deployment.
67	
68	## Reporting a vulnerability
69	
70	Please report suspected security issues privately to the maintainers rather than opening a
71	public issue.
72

76	document, not a certification), maintainers keep a separate compliance-posture register.*

**Two caveats kept deliberately.** These are largely **unpatched**, so "not impacted" rests on non-intersection and missing preconditions — there is nothing to bump, and no green audit will ever confirm this the way `pip-audit` confirms a CVE. name: project_redis7_pin_is_a_security_gate
description: DataQ's redis:7-alpine pin is a deliberate security gate, not staleness — Redis 8 bundles the Vector Sets module with an unpatched RCE (#980)

DataQ pins the Redis **server** image to `redis:7-alpine` in both `docker-compose.yml` and `deploy/terraform/azure/redis.tf` **on purpose**. Redis 8 bundles the Vector Sets module, whose duplicate-HNSW-ID `RESTORE` path is a full RCE (read oracle via `VLINKS ... WITHSCORES` → module-value overwrite → `freeModuleObject()` dispatch) with **no vendor fix** as of 2026-07-24. Redis 7 does not expose the `VSET`/`VLINKS` command surface at all. Tracked at [#980](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/980); found triaging `bikini/exploitarium`.

**Why:** upgrading to 8 would *add* the exposed surface, not remove it — the opposite of the usual "newer is safer" reflex. Nothing automated will raise this: `.github/dependabot.yml` covers pip/npm/github-actions only, **not Docker images**, so a server bump is always a deliberate human edit.

**How to apply:** before bumping the Redis server image to 8.x, verify with `MODULE LIST` on the running container that vector-sets is absent — do not assume the default. Keep `--requirepass` + `external_enabled = false` regardless (the PoC needs an authenticated client, so both layers would have to fail together). Do **not** confuse this with the separate, unrelated `redis` major-version ignore already in `dependabot.yml` — that one is **redis-py** (client), capped by `kombu[redis]`; this is the server image. Related: [[project_postgres_single_role_is_the_mitigation]].

name: project_postgres_single_role_is_the_mitigation
description: DataQ's single least-priv dataq_app Postgres role is a security control, not just tidiness — a second untrusted role in the dataq DB enables an unpatched RI cast escalation
metadata:
  type: project

DataQ's `dataq` database has exactly **one** app role (`dataq_app`, least-privilege, owns only that DB). That single-role model is **load-bearing security**, not housekeeping. PostgreSQL's referential-integrity check switches to the **referenced table's owner** before invoking an implicit cast on the FK value (`ri_triggers.c`), so a role that can `CREATE TYPE`/`FUNCTION`/`CAST` and holds `REFERENCES` on another owner's table runs its own SQL as that owner — reaching `COPY ... TO PROGRAM` if the owner has `pg_execute_server_program`. Unpatched upstream as of 2026-07-24; found triaging `bikini/exploitarium`. Documented in the `deploy/terraform/azure/postgres.tf` header and the guardrail table in `docs/progress.md`.

**Why:** adding a second, less-trusted role to the `dataq` database is what would *create* the exposure. There is no patch to wait for and no scanner that flags it — `pip-audit`/Dependabot see nothing, because the risk is a provisioning decision, not a dependency version.

**How to apply:** treat "provision another DB role in the `dataq` database" as a decision that needs revisiting this constraint, especially if multi-tenant or customer-facing DB access is ever considered. Deliberately **no GitHub issue** — it is a standing constraint with no schedulable work, unlike its sibling [[project_redis7_pin_is_a_security_gate]] which has a concrete trigger (#980).
